description: Grey granite plates held by unbroken salmon-pink seams. In armour a crushing blow arrives as a shove, a fall as a bruise.
lore: It is not one piece, and that is the trade of it: grey granite plates held each to each by salmon-pink seams, so it holds the way a wall holds — by how it is joined. Struck along a seam it opens into two clean plates that both still work; struck across the grain, gravel. Reading the pink before the hammer falls is a living in itself.

In armour it makes the ground feel closer: drops come off short, and what lands on you arrives without the part that was going to break something. The trade's sour rule holds here — stones off things that struck go into blades, and the stones that keep a person whole come off [[monsters/white_rabbit|a white creature]] that never struck first in its existence, and spent the whole of it on one question: where to be standing when something heavy happens.

[[characters/8c41be1e|Hearn]] wore one on the one organised walk anyone ever made on the cave. The others carried striking stones, and ribbed him the whole way east for armouring himself off a rabbit, and he let them. He came back alone, and unhollowed, and has never said whether the stone mattered inside. What is known is smaller: it has not been out of his plate since — not regraded, not repriced, not looked at.
gm_notes: If a player ever gets Hearn to say whether the stone mattered inside the cave, they have more than the Chronicle ever got. Do not sell that cheap.
